claim: The hierarchical ML model was made up of 16 individual multi-class classifiers, one per node.
source: This was made up of 16 individual multi-class classifiers, one per node (one root, four regional, 11 sub-regional).

claim: The hierarchical model included one root classifier, four regional classifiers, and 11 sub-regional classifiers.
source: This was made up of 16 individual multi-class classifiers, one per node (one root, four regional, 11 sub-regional).

claim: Sample classification was performed using a top-down approach where samples are first classified at the root node into 'regions'.
source: Sample classification was performed using a top-down approach, where samples are first classified at the root node into 'regions' (e.g. Africa) then, if the predicted probability is greater than a minimum threshold value (0.5), samples are passed to the appropriate regional node to be classified into a nested subset of 'subregions' (e.g. Northern Africa) and finally passed to a subregional node where they are classified into a nested subset of 'countries' (e.g. Egypt) (Figure 2A).
evidence: This is a direct description of the classification methodology.

claim: Samples are passed to the next hierarchical level only if the predicted probability is greater than a minimum threshold value of 0.5.
source: Sample classification was performed using a top-down approach, where samples are first classified at the root node into 'regions' (e.g. Africa) then, if the predicted probability is greater than a minimum threshold value (0.5), samples are passed to the appropriate regional node to be classified into a nested subset of 'subregions' (e.g. Northern Africa) and finally passed to a subregional node where they are classified into a nested subset of 'countries' (e.g. Egypt) (Figure 2A).
evidence: This is a direct description of the classification methodology.

claim: The model was trained on filtered unitig patterns (presence-absence) generated from quality-controlled genomic short-read data files.
source: For rapid and minimal sample processing and to provide end-to-end sample classification directly from the sequencer, the model was trained on filtered unitig patterns (presence-absence) generated from quality-controlled genomic short-read data files.
